item.text: {"question_id":"3B.1","answer":"During 2023, Germany maintained substantial formal protection against the gravest state abuses: the U.S. State Department reported no government or agent arbitrary killings, disappearances, political prisoners, or credible official torture, and said arrest safeguards and judicial independence were generally respected (BATCH-0009-E014). Courts also corrected disproportionate searches and unlawful detention practices, including 2023 Federal Constitutional Court decisions and Federal Supreme Court detention rulings (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0025-E018; BATCH-0011-R05-E012). These remedies show that legal safeguards could operate, but they also expose recurring implementation failures. In detention pending removal, Federal Supreme Court decisions included 2023 findings involving denial of a lawyer’s opportunity to attend a hearing and insufficient justification of detention duration; a nonrepresentative law-firm sample of 2,458 represented cases from 2001 through October 2023 found 1,283 (52.2%) unlawful, with affected clients detained an average of 25.8 days (BATCH-0011-R05-E012). The asylum system also used practices later found unlawful: the Federal Administrative Court ruled BAMF mobile-device screening illegal where less intrusive identity checks were available (BATCH-0011-R01-E016). During 2023, Dublin appeals faced a difficult one-week deadline without automatic suspensive effect, and the report described practical difficulty obtaining an effective remedy; it also described allegations that detention orders were sometimes made without required conditions, while the cited 2023 restraint figure is not fully reproduced in the supplied excerpt (BATCH-0011-R02-E006). As of 31 December 2023, a detention provision lacked safeguards for vulnerable groups according to NGO criticism, although the provision predated Scholz’s term (BATCH-0011-R05-E007). Vulnerability protection was also incomplete: identification was described as inconsistent and not systematically monitored, and documented cases showed trauma or explicit torture references did not trigger consultation with special officers; BAMF did not record consultation or handover rates (BATCH-0011-R03-E002; BATCH-0011-R03-E007). Police accountability remained a material concern: a 2023 report of 2021 data found more than 90% of 2,790 police-use-of-force investigations were discontinued and only 2% led to charges, while the underlying study was nonrepresentative and the figures predated 2023 (BATCH-0006-E008). In April 2023, Berlin police investigated an officer’s pain grip against a peaceful protester and a bodily-harm complaint was filed, but no final outcome is supplied (BATCH-0006-E010). The evidence therefore supports a mixed 2023 assessment: meaningful national legal protection and functioning judicial correction coexisted with recurring arbitrary-detention, due-process, vulnerability-protection, police-force, and remedy gaps. The adverse incidents concern federal, Länder, local, police, BAMF, and court institutions; none is shown to have been personally ordered by Scholz. The severity is recurring institutional failure and isolated documented force, not systematic repression or state terror. Open reporting improves visibility, but underreporting—including fear of police reactions among LGBTQI* respondents—means absence of complaints or reported torture cannot establish complete protection
